answer.rationale: Current churn pressure is on price-sensitive SMB, a segment where exp_73 showed promotional pricing drives short-term signup but fails at renewal—exactly the cohort now at risk. Deploying another discount would repeat that failure pattern and train price sensitivity deeper into the base. Instead, redirect focus to enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44: enterprise converts better through sales-assisted flows with superior pipeline quality) and strengthen the self-serve path with activation_messaging (memory_91: improved week-one engagement) and onboarding simplification (memory_86: lifted early adoption). This three-part approach: (1) shifts revenue mix toward higher-LTV enterprise accounts less vulnerable to competitive discounting, (2) hardens retention and engagement in remaining SMB through product-side improvements, (3) avoids the renewal cliff that killed value in the last discount cohort. The enterprise move is not reactive pricing but structural—it rebalances the customer base toward sustainable segments. Standard experiment scope preserves the option to adjust if churn accelerates unexpectedly, while allowing enterprise motion to compound through the sales cycle.
